tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Local sections of a submersion]

↗ prop:local-section-euclidean ↗ thm:inverse-function-theorem-manifolds

Let $\pi : M \to N$ be a smooth map of smooth manifolds, with $M$ modelled on a boundaryless model. If $d\pi _p$ is surjective, then there is $\sigma : N \to M$, smooth at $\pi (p)$, with $\sigma (\pi (p)) = p$ and $\pi (\sigma (y)) = y$ for every $y$ near $\pi (p)$.

Proof

↗ prop:local-section-euclidean Write $\varphi $ for the chart of $M$ at $p$, $\psi $ for the chart of $N$ at $\pi (p)$, $a = \varphi (p)$, and $F = \psi \circ \pi \circ \varphi ^{-1}$ for the chart representation. Then $F$ is $C^\infty $ at $a$, and $d\pi _p$ *is* $dF_a$ read through the charts, so $dF_a$ is surjective. Proposition 4 gives a local section $\sigma _E$ of $F$ through $a$; set $\sigma = \varphi ^{-1} \circ \sigma _E \circ \psi $.

Then $\sigma (\pi (p)) = \varphi ^{-1}(\sigma _E(F(a))) = \varphi ^{-1}(a) = p$, and $\sigma $ is smooth at $\pi (p)$ as a composite of $\psi $, $\sigma _E$ and $\varphi ^{-1}$ — the last being smooth on the chart target, which is a neighbourhood of $a$ because the model is boundaryless. For $y$ near $\pi (p)$, $F(\sigma _E(\psi (y))) = \psi (y)$, which unwinds to $\psi (\pi (\sigma (y))) = \psi (y)$; since $\pi (\sigma (y))$ and $y$ both lie in the chart domain for $y$ near $\pi (p)$, and $\psi $ is injective there, $\pi (\sigma (y)) = y$.

□
